assumptions.description: Assume $A=A^{\mathsf T}\in\mathbb R^{d\times d}$ with spectrum in $[a,b_{\mathrm{spec}}]$, $\|A\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\Lambda$, and $b\in\mathbb R^d\setminus\{0\}$. The function $h$ satisfies $|h(x)|\le C_h$ on the extended interval $[a-\eta,b_{\mathrm{spec}}+\eta]$, where $0<\eta\le\|A\|_{\mathrm{op}}$.
assumptions.scope: Each fixed admissible input and its entire query domain

description_paragraphs: The base loss is $\|\widehat{y}-h(A)b\|_2/\|b\|_2$ with threshold $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{out}}$. Define $\delta_k=\inf_{\deg q<k}\max_{x\in[a-\eta,b_{\mathrm{spec}}+\eta]}|q(x)-h(x)|$, the polynomial-approximation error in the source bound.

source_fields.finiteness_conditions: The matrix is finite-dimensional and satisfies the model's spectral, norm, and function assumptions. Zero denominators and zero optimal error follow the conventions explicitly stated here.

auxiliary_interfaces.description: A public auxiliary scalar-function interface. Complete definitions and charges appear in operations.

description_paragraphs: Spectral bounds, $h,b,\Lambda,\eta,C_h$, and the target error are public. Floating-point operations follow the source relative-rounding model with unit roundoff $u$ and no overflow or underflow. Products satisfy $\|\operatorname{fl}(Av)-Av\|_2\le2d^{3/2}\|A\|_{\mathrm{op}}\|v\|_2u$ for each vector; exact $Av$ is not supplied.

A public scalar-function interface evaluates $h(x)$ to relative accuracy $u$ on the extended spectral interval: $|\operatorname{fl}(h(x))-h(x)|\le u|h(x)|$. This is the implementation assumption in Section 5. Count these calls separately as $N_h$; the running time of an expensive scalar function is not implicitly constant.
source_fields.description_zh: The spectral bounds, $h,b,\Lambda,\eta,C_h$, and target error are public. Floating-point arithmetic follows the source relative-rounding model with unit roundoff $u$ and no overflow or underflow. Matrix products satisfy $\|\operatorname{fl}(Av)-Av\|_2\le2d^{3/2}\|A\|_{\mathrm{op}}\|v\|_2u$ for each vector; the interface does not supply exact $Av$. The public scalar-function interface computes $h(x)$ on the extended spectral interval to relative accuracy $u$: $|\operatorname{fl}(h(x))-h(x)|\le u|h(x)|$. This is the implementation assumption in Section 5 of the source. Its calls are counted separately as $N_h$; evaluating an expensive scalar function is not assumed to take constant time.

operations.coupling: One fixed matrix; repeated queries are allowed
operations.index_control: The algorithm selects queries; the matrix is fixed throughout the instance, and repeated queries are permitted.

operations.coupling: The same public scalar-function interface is used throughout. Each response obeys the stated relative rounding-error bound.

source_fields.budget_semantics: fixed worst-case joint budget; no expectation substituted

components.description: Effective mantissa bits used throughout the algorithm. This is a joint-resource coordinate, not a sum over calls or a count of bit operations.

description_paragraphs: The joint resource is $(N_{\mathrm{mv}},b_{\mathrm{fp}},N_h)$. There are at most $k$ approximate matrix-vector products. The specified postprocessing evaluates $h$ at at most $k$ tridiagonal eigenvalues, hence $N_h\le k$. The quantity $b_{\mathrm{fp}}$ is the effective mantissa precision for the entire run.

The three quantities remain independent resource coordinates. The source gives sufficient mantissa precision, and the scalar-function interface must additionally attain the stated relative evaluation error. Full arithmetic or bit-operation time depends on the implementation.
source_fields.description_zh: The joint resources are $(N_{\mathrm{mv}},b_{\mathrm{fp}},N_h)$: at most k approximate matrix-vector products, and scalar evaluation of h on at most k tridiagonal eigenvalues, so $N_h\le k$. The quantity $b_{\mathrm{fp}}$ is the effective mantissa length for the run. These coordinates remain separate. The theorem supplies sufficient precision, while scalar evaluations must meet their stated relative error. Full arithmetic or bit runtime depends on implementation.
source_fields.precision_model: finite precision under explicit roundoff conditions

description_paragraphs: Compute the Lanczos approximation $\widehat y$ to $h(A)b$ in the specified floating-point model.

algorithms.adaptivity: arbitrary unless fixed algorithm is explicitly declared
description_paragraphs: Use the source k-step finite-precision Lanczos algorithm with Gu-Eisenstat tridiagonal eigendecomposition. Adding full reorthogonalization changes the algorithm and its guarantee. Rounding follows Requirement 1 and the matrix-product error assumptions.

algorithms.parallelism: Block calls are charged by column; no separate communication-round budget is imposed.

guarantees.complete_expression: For every fixed admissible input and arithmetic error satisfying the stated rounding model, the source gives a deterministic action-error bound. There is no private randomness or success-probability parameter.
